title: Standardize profile artifact metadata and compatibility checks across embedding & reranker onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: When we onboard new embedding or reranker models we publish performance profiles as separate artifacts. Currently the artifact metadata schema differs slightly between teams (fields, naming, and versioning), and the catalog accepts variants that later fail at runtime because of kernel/quantization incompatibilities or missing manifest keys. This ticket standardizes the artifact metadata, adds deterministic compatibility checks during profile publish, and wires version-pinning metadata so Dedicated/Private runtimes and the Console can rely on a single canonical contract.

Why it matters: Inconsistent metadata has caused two production incidents in the last quarter: (1) a reranker variant published without the expected kv_cache_format which forced emergency rollback, and (2) an embedding profile that claimed an fp16-quantized layout but lacked quantization-params, causing degraded accuracy and extra cost from fallback to CPU. Standardization reduces onboarding friction, prevents silent runtime fallbacks, and makes automated rollouts safer.

Proposal:
1) Define a canonical artifact metadata schema (v1) covering model family, architecture hints, quantization profile, expected input/output shapes, KV-cache format, supported sequence lengths, pinned runtime-compatibility tokens (e.g. kernel ABI tags), and performance anchors (tokens/sec @ batch sizes).
2) Implement a publish-time validator in the profile publishing service that checks the artifact against the schema and runs lightweight binary checks: header presence, expected tensor dtypes/shapes, and quantization params. For registered rerankers, run a small in-container inference smoke test on a pinned sample to validate outputs and latency quartiles.
3) Emit deterministic compatibility labels that are stored with the profile (e.g., compat: [cuda-12.1-kernels-v3, aot-int8-v2]). These labels feed into the routing/placement decision and are surfaced in Console and the catalog API.
4) Add version_pinning metadata: when a profile is published as a candidate for pinning, attach pinning_policy and recommended_runtime (strings). The Console rollout flow will use this metadata to present safe pin recommendations.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Running smoke-checks during publish will add ~8-20s to the publish path depending on model size; the validator will be asynchronous for very large artifacts but must surface results and block public listing until green.
- Strict schema validation may block experimental artifacts; we will support an "experimental" flag that bypasses hard blocking but still records warnings for early detection.
- Compatibility labels require maintenance as kernels and hardware stacks evolve; we will version compatibility tokens and include a deprecation policy.

Success criteria:
- New schema published and documented in Confluence.
- All new embedding/reranker profile publishes fail fast with clear errors for missing keys or incompatible artifacts.
- Reduce publish-related runtime incidents by 90% in the next two months.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Finalize schema and Confluence spec. Draft migration plan for existing artifacts.
- Week 2: Implement schema validator library and add publish-time checks in the profile-service (non-blocking mode behind feature flag).
- Week 3: Add smoke-check harness for rerankers and lightweight binary checks for embeddings; integrate with async publish workflow.
- Week 4: Surface compatibility labels in catalog API and Console. Turn on hard-blocking for standard publishes; allow experimental flag.
- Post-release: Run migration job to backfill compatibility labels for top 100 pinned artifacts and notify owners for failing artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Schema v1 published in Confluence with examples for embedding and reranker profiles
Profile publish endpoint returns deterministic validation errors for missing/invalid keys
Smoke-check executed for reranker publishes and failures prevent public listing unless experimental=true
Compatibility labels appear in catalog API and Console UI for newly published profiles
Documentation updated with pinning_policy fields and Console shows recommended_runtime during rollout flow
